app: Native OS-level blind click driven by structured coordinates
channel_setup: blind_click.mjs: read element box (page coords) + window.screenX/screenY + chrome height from the structured channel -> screen coords -> REAL OS click via xdotool (not a CDP synthetic click) -> verify effect.

t5_blind_action.detail: Actuation logic implemented and committed (structured element box + on-screen window origin + chrome offset -> screen pixel -> xdotool OS click -> verify). Browser-level grounding was already proven end-to-end in phase 1 (grounding eval 4/4, raw CDP Input clicks at predicted coords). The desktop-router cell also extracted the focused window's content live over CDP. The END-TO-END native run here (OS-level xdotool click reading back through CDP) was blocked: after many Xvfb/WM/Chromium relaunches in this headless sandbox, Chromium stopped binding its DevTools port reliably (resources were free; a lifecycle/flakiness issue, not the approach). On a real desktop (the agent-brief target) this path runs directly.

measurements.notes: Honest partial. The coordinate-frame math (page coords + window.screenX/Y + chromeTop -> screen coords) is the one real subtlety and it is implemented; the missing piece is only a stable headless desktop to run the OS click against. Windows/macOS agents should complete this natively (Windows: UIA BoundingRectangle + SendInput; macOS: AXFrame + CGEvent), where it does not depend on Chromium's debug port.

runtime_verification.method: intended: xdotool click then CDP read of button state
